_note: Build page parts list. 'bought' is changed only by pull request, from a Discord part update. Run python3 tools/embed_build_parts.py after editing.

v1.name: V1: line follower
v1.how: Follows a tape line down the hallway, counts junction and door marks to know where it is, and stops at the chosen room.
v1.can: Room-to-room trips sent from the site. Stops for anything in front of it (single depth sensor). Physical E-stop.
v1.cant: Leave the tape, or recover if it loses count.

v2.name: V2: room scanner
v2.how: Drives the hallway like a real car (it steers; it can't spin in place). At stops, a roof turret sweeps the depth sensor to match the scan to the saved map, and the camera in the windshield reads room markers to confirm where it is.
v2.can: Room-to-room trips from the site with no tape. Gyro heading. Stops for obstacles even without Wi-Fi (the turret faces forward while driving). Stops instead of guessing when unsure. Physical E-stop.
v2.cant: See into rooms (about 2 to 3 m range), recognize people specifically, or turn in place.
v2.catch: Permission to place room markers, and the parts fit confirmed.

parts.what: World's Littlest Waymo Jaguar I-PACE diecast. The body and glass; the base and wheels may be replaced.
parts.note: On hand. Outside 112 x 45.6 x 51.2 mm (Waymo shop; height includes the roof dome), about 1:42 scale. Isabel is measuring the inside with calipers.

parts.what: 1/43 4WD mini RC drift car (Dingdongwu, on Amazon). Gives the drive motor, steering, gears, wheels and battery (check the battery has its own protection board).
parts.note: Ordered by Noah, arriving Fri 11/06. Steers with a front servo or a left/center/right coil, so it can't turn in place. Confirm on teardown.

parts.what: The car's brain and camera. Runs motors, safety stop and marker reading. The camera pokes through the windshield, facing forward.
parts.note: An ESP32-C3 is on hand for bench tests only (no camera).

parts.what: Small driver (DRV8835 class) for the drive motor. The steering servo runs straight from the ESP32.
parts.note: DRV8833 on hand (BJ). Channel B steers if the donor's steering is a coil.

parts.what: Tiny slide switch plus a tether or pull-pin that cuts motor power without Wi-Fi.
Small piezo sounder for the chime (a must) and 2 amber LEDs with resistors (lowest priority).
parts.note: LEDs and resistors on hand; piezo to buy.

parts.what: Steadies the power when the motors start, so the ESP32 doesn't reset.
Fits inside the shell; normal hookup wire is too thick.
Insulates the electronics from the metal diecast shell.
3D printed chassis to hold the parts, the roof turret dome, and printed markers for the rooms.
Opens the diecast to get the body off its base.
Measures motor start-up and stall current.
Gives the car its own Wi-Fi in the hallway if campus Wi-Fi blocks it.
Small reflectance sensor under the car to follow the tape.
parts.note: KY-033 line sensor and two IR sensors on hand (Noah), tested on an ESP32.

parts.what: Cheap front distance sensor (VL53L0X or VL53L1X class) to stop for obstacles.
8 x 8 depth grid in a cone of about 60 degrees, 2 to 3 m indoors. Rides the roof turret: faces forward while driving to stop for obstacles, sweeps at stops to scan.
Tracks the car's heading between scans and on turns.
parts.note: Skip if the donor's gyro can be used.

parts.what: Sweeps the depth sensor from a printed roof dome, like a real Waymo's lidar. Sweeps back and forth rather than spinning, so no slip ring. Needed because the drift car can't turn in place.
parts.note: 2 g 180-degree micro servo, JST version. Being ordered by Subir.
